title: SRE weekly: Signal Cafe — 2029-12-18
content:
Purpose
Quick-weekly standup dump from the SRE Signal Cafe. Triage notes, short incident summaries, SLO trends, on-call handoff points, and open hypotheses we want to test next sprint. Intended for the ops triage channel and Eng leadership read-ahead.

Highlights (TL;DR)
- Incident curve: 3 customer-facing incidents this week; two were transient model-serving spikes, one was a cache invalidation bug that caused 15–30s tail latency for ~5% of requests for ~42 minutes (see INC-SRE-719).
- SLO snapshot: overall write/read token p95 latency is up 8% week-over-week; error budget burn on the hosted API remains low but dedicated pools saw a small increase tied to scheduled quantization rollout (see JIRA-SRE-4190).
- Operational priorities: (1) stabilize cache invalidation gating in runtime (short patch landed), (2) refine autoscale trigger to reduce oscillation in dedicated pools, (3) create a lightweight chaos test for prefix-cache eviction.

Incident summaries (short)
1) INC-SRE-719 — cache-invalidation cascade (2029-12-16 04:12 UTC)
   - What happened: A race in the prefix cache invalidation path triggered eviction for active sessions during a rolling rollback. Affected requests hit the cold KV path and inflated tail latency.
   - Impact: 15–30s tail latency for ~4.7% of requests to hosted/text-generation-v2 for ~42 minutes. No data loss. Some customer SDKs retried aggressively leading to higher downstream load.
   - Mitigation: Revert of the invalidation gating change and a hotfix to add an additional semaphore around cache eviction; traffic gradually normalized.
   - Follow-ups: Postmortem draft assigned to Liam (JIRA-SRE-4127). Action: add guardrails to prevent invalidation during active rollouts and add a synthetic test that exercises concurrent invalidation+generation.

2) INC-SRE-723 — scheduled quantization rollout caused increased error rate (2029-12-14 21:00 UTC)
   - What happened: A canary quantized model variant’s upstream fallback logic was miswired so that in cases of moderate batch-skipping, requests were routed to an incompatible kernel leading to 500s for a small subset.
   - Impact: ~0.6% error spike on dedicated pools during the 2 hour window; noticed by internal smoke checks and customer page.
   - Mitigation: Canary halted; traffic shifted to non-quantized variant; patch to kernel-compat routing merged (PR linked).
   - Follow-ups: Add a kernel compatibility matrix to our model onboarding checklist and make the canary gating stricter (automated replay + golden-corpus checks).

3) INC-SRE-726 — health-check flapping due to noisy GPU driver update (2029-12-12 09:30 UTC)
   - What happened: New driver rolled to a subset of dedicated hosts; some subtle NVLINK recoveries caused transient health-check failures.
   - Impact: Several pods restarted, brief capacity reduction (handled by autoscale). No customer-visible errors beyond small latency blips.
   - Mitigation: Reverted driver on affected fleet; vendor engaged.
   - Follow-ups: Add tooling to correlate driver version + health-check metrics automatically and add a staging gate for driver rollouts.

SLOs & Metrics snapshot (end-of-week)
- Hosted API p95 generation latency: 290ms (last week 268ms) — +8%
- Dedicated pools p95: 320ms (last week 300ms) — +6.7%; increased variance during quantization rollout window
- Error budget burn (30d rolling): Hosted API 2.8%, Dedicated 6.2%
- Alert churn: 14 alerts triggered this week down from 21 (good)

On-call handoff notes (incoming shift)
- Active issues: INC-SRE-719 (cache invalidation) — follow the postmortem checklist, verify the semaphore patch in canary prior to broad rollout.
- Runbooks to watch: "cache-eviction-gate" and "model-canary-fallback" — both were exercised this week; update step #3 in the canary runbook to include kernel compatibility check.
- Escalation path tweak: For model-serving tail-latency incidents, escalate directly to runtime-eng on-call after the initial triage if p95 stays >600ms for >10m. Documented in confluence link.

Operational hypotheses & experiments (proposal)
- Hypothesis A: A lightweight prefix-cache chaos test that evicts cached prefixes randomly under load will surface the race earlier. Experiment: build a chaos script run in staging that evicts 1–2% of active prefixes every 10s for 30 minutes and observe tail. Owner: Marco.
- Hypothesis B: Autoscale oscillation in dedicated pools correlates with our batch size thresholds when quantized kernels are used. Experiment: Run localized load tests toggling batch target and quantization profile. Owner: Aisha.
- Hypothesis C: A small client-side retry jitter can reduce amplification from retries during tail spikes. Quick experiment: change SDK retry jitter logic behind a feature flag for a small cohort. Owner: Taylor.

Action items (next 7 days)
- Liam: Finish INC-SRE-719 postmortem draft and circulate by 2029-12-20. (JIRA-SRE-4127)
- Marco: Prototype prefix-cache-chaos script and run in staging by 2029-12-22.
- Aisha: Run autoscale/batch experiments; report observations at next Signal Cafe.
- Taylor: Create SDK feature-flag for randomized retry jitter; small cohort rollout by 2029-12-26.
- Priya: Schedule an ops/lab sync with runtime-eng and product-hosted-api to align on canary policy (2029-12-21).

Notes to self / informal observations
- We’re seeing repeated incidents that center around rollout surface area (cache invalidation, quantization rollout, driver updates). Need a short checklist for any change that touches request-path or binary/kernel changes.
- The on-call deck felt efficient this week — could be due to lower noise from APM changes; keep the current alert threshold for memory-pressure alerts but re-evaluate after autoscale experiments.
- A few customers pinged about intermittent timeouts — likely correlated to cache invalidation window; include a short blurb in customer-success weekly with mitigations we took.

Open questions (unresolved)
- Should we adopt a staged invalidation approach (per-tenant or per-session) to avoid global eviction during rollouts? Pros/cons + implementation cost needed.
- Do we want an automated rollback trigger if a canary increases p95 by >25% for 10m, or should we keep manual judgement for the moment?

Attachments / links in this doc
- INC-SRE-719 notes: confluence://sre/incidents/719
- Postmortem draft link (internal): confluence://sre/postmortems/719-draft
- Autoscale experiment board: confluence://sre/experiments/autoscale-2029-12
- Infra PR that fixed kernel routing: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/874

Reminder: Next Signal Cafe is 2029-12-25 (light week) — skip if no material items. If someone wants to prep a short demo of the prefix-cache chaos experiment, ping me off-channel.

-- Priya
